headline.label: Usability score
headline.sentence: 4 of 12 people passed every check in all three tasks. No pass mark was agreed, so there is nothing to compare it with yet.

sections.heading: What we measured
paragraphs: 12 people tried three tasks in the online shop. They checked out an item, found the nearest store and started a return.
For each task we noted whether the person finished. Each person also rated how easy the task was, how quick it felt and how satisfied they were.

sections.heading: Your result
paragraphs: The usability score is 33%. It is the share of people who passed every check in every task they tried: 4 of 12 people passed everything.
A person passes a task only when they finish it and rate ease, speed and satisfaction high enough. One weak rating in one task is enough to fail.
No pass mark was agreed for this score. So it is not above or below any target. The true share is most likely between 14% and 61%.

sections.heading: What the score is made of
paragraphs: Each task has its own score, built from four checks. The checks have no targets of their own, so we give the plain numbers.
Finding the nearest store scored 75%. Checking out scored 58%. Starting a return scored 42%.

items.label: Add to cart & checkout
items.text: 10 of 12 people finished. 7 of 12 people rated ease 4 or higher. 10 of 12 people rated the speed 3 or higher. 9 of 12 people rated satisfaction 4 or higher.

items.label: Find nearest store
items.text: 11 of 12 people finished. 10 of 12 people rated ease 4 or higher. 11 of 12 people rated the speed 3 or higher. 10 of 12 people rated satisfaction 4 or higher.

items.label: Start a return
items.text: 7 of 12 people finished. 5 of 12 people rated ease 4 or higher. 9 of 12 people rated the speed 3 or higher. 7 of 12 people rated satisfaction 4 or higher.

sections.heading: How sure we are
paragraphs: With 12 people, the true overall share is most likely between 14% and 61%. That is a wide range.
The task scores are just as loose. For starting a return, the true score is most likely between 19% and 68%.
More people would narrow these ranges. That matters most once a pass mark is set and the score must be judged against it.

sections.heading: What to fix first
paragraphs: Start a return is the weakest task. Only 5 of 12 people rated it easy enough, and only 7 of 12 people finished.
In checkout, ease is also the weakest part: 7 of 12 people rated it 4 or higher. Look at where people hesitated in both tasks.
Finding the nearest store works best. Its weakest part is satisfaction, with 10 of 12 people rating it 4 or higher.

sections.heading: What this number cannot tell you
paragraphs: The score shows how many people got through everything. It does not say why the others struggled. Watch the recordings to find out.
Measured time does not enter this score. It uses how quick the task felt, not the stopwatch. The time targets and the satisfaction target are not used either.
The result covers these three tasks and these 12 people only. Other tasks or other customers may do better or worse.
The answer depends on the scoring method. The next section explains why.

sections.heading: Would another method change the answer?
paragraphs: Yes, by a lot. Other methods give partial credit on each part instead of pass or fail, so they score higher.

The original four-part score, which also counts mistakes, gives 75%. The three-part version without mistakes gives 72%. Averaging the parts' percentages gives 68%. Setting time targets from how long satisfied people took gives 63%.
This study is a go or no-go decision. For that, the pass or fail share fits best. It asks how many people had a good enough experience on every check, and a high average cannot hide one failed check.
Before the next round, agree a pass mark for this share. Then the score can be judged as clearly above or below it.

glossary.definition: The share of people who passed every check in every task they tried.
One thing a person must get right in a task: finish it, and rate ease, speed and satisfaction high enough.
The share agreed in advance that the score must reach for the product to pass.
The values the true score most likely falls between, given how few people took part.
